scolopsis_bimaculata.distribution: East and West coasts of India
field_marks: Blue stripe joining the eyes
1–2 brownish blotches on the upper body
Colour: upper body grey, whitish below, with a blue stripe joining the eyes
Body shape fusiform / normal; cross-section oval
Large suborbital spine present
Antrorse (forward-directed) suborbital spine absent
Head scales reach forward to the posterior nostrils
Lower limb of preopercle scaly
Pelvic fins long, reaching between anus and anal-fin origin; axillary scale present

atule_mate.distribution: Tamil Nadu and Kerala coasts and the Andamans; also Chilika Lake and the Godavari estuary
field_marks: Olive-green back shading to silvery-white belly
Black spot, slightly smaller than the eye, on the upper edge of the gill cover
Dorsal and tail fins dusky greenish-yellow; anal fin pale yellow
Last dorsal and anal rays finlet-like but attached (no separate finlets)
36–49 bony scutes on the straight rear part of the lateral line
Adipose eyelid covers the eye except for a vertical slit over the pupil

lutjanus_quinquelineatus.distribution: Indian seas; Indo-West Pacific from the Persian Gulf to Fiji
field_marks: Bright yellow body, fins yellow too
Series of blue horizontal stripes along the side
Round black spot, eye-sized or larger, below the front soft dorsal rays, mostly above the lateral line
Steeply sloping head profile
Clear notch and knob on the rear edge of the gill-cover bone
Tail nearly squared off (truncate)

megalaspis_cordyla.distribution: Coastal waters of India; also Chilika Lake (Odisha)
field_marks: Slender torpedo-shaped body; bluish-grey to green back, silvery sides and belly, dark fins
Large black spot on the upper rear edge of the gill cover
Row of separate finlets behind the dorsal (7–9) and anal (8–10) fins
Very large, strong scutes (51–59) along the whole lateral line
Strongly flattened tail stalk with a central keel; forked tail
Adipose eyelid covers the eye except for a vertical slit

charybdis_natator.distribution: Indo-West Pacific, from the Red Sea to China and Australia; fished commercially in India
field_marks: Orange-red overall; ridges on the carapace and legs dark reddish brown
Carapace covered in very short fur, except on several bare, granular ridges running across its front half
Carapace up to about 17 cm wide
Lives on rocky, sandy or muddy bottoms and near coral reefs

decapterus_russelli.distribution: Indo-West Pacific, from East Africa to Japan and Australia; the most common Decapterus in Indian Ocean coastal waters
field_marks: Bluish-green back, silvery below
Small black spot on the gill cover
Lateral line curves down below the soft dorsal fin, with 30–44 strong scutes
Tail fin clear to yellowish
Soft dorsal and anal fins low, not sickle-shaped; pectoral fin slightly sickle-shaped
Snout longer than the eye

escualosa_thoracata.distribution: Northern Indian Ocean from Karachi to Myanmar, east to Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Australia
field_marks: Small, up to about 10 cm
Bright, broad silver stripe along the flank
Belly strongly keeled; body flattened side to side
Second bone above the upper jaw (supra-maxilla) almost rectangular
No spines in the dorsal or anal fins
Schools in shallow coastal water; juveniles enter river mouths

lutjanus_vitta.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Seychelles, then southern India to New Caledonia, north to the Ryukyu Islands
field_marks: Whitish or pink body with a yellowish-brown to black stripe along the middle of the side
Adults have yellow dorsal, anal and tail fins
Juveniles: intensely black mid-side stripe with an eye-sized oval black spot below the last dorsal spines
Scale rows above the lateral line rise obliquely
Head profile moderately sloped; notch and knob on the gill-cover bone poorly developed

nemipterus_bipunctatus.distribution: Indian Ocean: Red Sea and East Africa to the Arabian Sea, Sri Lanka, Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea
field_marks: Upper body pinkish, silvery below
Two faint stripes on the snout
No spine below the eye (suborbital spine absent)
Long pelvic fins, reaching to or just past the start of the anal fin
Pectoral fins reach to or just behind the anus
Lives on sand or mud bottoms

pelates_quadrilineatus.distribution: Indo-West Pacific, from the Red Sea and East Africa to southern Japan, New Guinea and the Arafura Sea
field_marks: Silvery body with 4–6 dark horizontal stripes
A black blotch behind the head below the dorsal-fin origin, sometimes another in front of the dorsal fin
Tail fin pale or slightly dusky
12–13 dorsal spines
Common in estuaries and brackish water; croaks when taken out of the water

pomadasys_maculatus.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: throughout the Indian Ocean, north to China and south to Australia
field_marks: Several large, dark, elongated blotches on the upper back, one forming a saddle on the nape
Moderately deep body
Two pairs of small pores on the chin
12 dorsal spines
Found over sand near reefs in coastal waters

rastrelliger_kanagurta.distribution: Indo-West Pacific, from South Africa, the Red Sea and East Africa to Indonesia, China, Australia and Samoa
field_marks: Black spot on the body near the lower edge of the pectoral fin
Head longer than the body is deep
Upper jaw partly hidden under the cheek bone, reaching about the rear edge of the eye
Very long, bristly gill rakers
Anal spine rudimentary
Schools in plankton-rich coastal bays and lagoons

scolopsis_vosmeri.distribution: Northern Indian Ocean, from Pakistan, western India and Sri Lanka through the Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea to western Indonesia
field_marks: Most body scales with a black spot; tail stalk white
Broad white bar from the nape onto the gill cover, and a white patch below the eye
Dorsal, anal and pelvic fins crimson or orange-red
Large backward-pointing spine below the eye, with a small forward-pointing spine just above it
Second anal-fin spine longer and stronger than the first and third
Juveniles lack the nape bar and have a dark-edged white band from behind the eye to the tail stalk

selar_crumenophthalmus.distribution: Circumtropical; in the Indo-Pacific from East Africa to southern Japan, Hawaii and New Caledonia
field_marks: Very large eye, almost fully covered by a fatty (adipose) eyelid
Metallic blue or blue-green back, silver or white below
Yellow stripe (may be absent) from the top of the gill opening to the tail stalk
Black spot on the edge of the gill cover
Deep furrow on the shoulder girdle with a large bump just above it
29–42 small scutes on the lateral line; first two anal spines detached

sphyraena_obtusata.distribution: Indo-Pacific, from the Red Sea and East Africa to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Australia
field_marks: Long, nearly cylindrical body with small scales; long, pointed head
Large horizontal mouth with the lower jaw sticking out
Green above, silvery below
First dorsal fin starts slightly before the tip of the pectoral fin
Pelvic fins well ahead of the pectoral-fin tip
Schools in bays, estuaries, seagrass beds and rocky reefs

stolephorus_indicus.distribution: Indian Ocean, from the Red Sea to Ranong and Phuket, Thailand
field_marks: Slender, elongate body, fairly round in cross-section, with a silver stripe along the flank
Light, translucent fleshy-brown colour
No dark pigment lines on the back between head and dorsal fin
2–6 small needle-like scutes on the belly in front of the pelvic fins
Short upper jaw with a pointed tip, reaching only to the front edge of the pre-gill cover
Anal fin starts below the middle of the dorsal fin

terapon_jarbua.distribution: Indo-Pacific, from the Red Sea and East Africa to Samoa, north to southern Japan, south to Australia
field_marks: Oblong body, moderately flattened side to side
Lower spine on the gill cover extends well beyond the gill-cover flap
Exposed bone above the gill cover, serrated at the rear
Tail fin slightly notched (emarginate)
Shallow sandy bottoms near river mouths; juveniles and adults also in fresh water
